pl295231.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl295231.description: This site, discussed in scholarly literature in the 20th century, seems from satellite imagery to have been impinged or destroyed in the construction of the Rocade Tipaza/Autoroute Tipaza - Cherchel in the early years of the 21st century. It seems to have been a villa with a central courtyard and primary entrance facing east, with a row of rooms with arched openings overlooking the wadi to the north. Vats and presses, possibly for processing grapes for wine, were discovered. Anselmino hypothesized that another, unexcavated structure immediately to the east was a church.

pl973087402.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl973087402.description: A prehistoric settlement covering some 10 hectares with evidence for approximately 150 huts located in Selargius, Sardinia.

pl991190962.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl991190962.description: The Necropolis of Montessu is located near Villaperuccio, Sardinia. It is the site of about 40 domus de Janas tombs and dates to the third millennium B.C.

pl492787885.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl492787885.description: A pre-nuragic village of the Ozieri culture and later nuraghe located in the Laguna di Santa Gilla.

pl444064177.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl444064177.description: Pranu Muttedu is a pre- and protohistoric archaeological site located near Goni, Sardinia. The complex includes standing stones (menhirs) and prehistoric built tombs (domus de janas). The site dates to the Late Neolithic (3200 – 2800 BC) and Early Chalcolithic (2800 – 2600 BC) periods.

pl828393338.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl828393338.description: At Capocorb Vell are the remains of a Talaiotic settlement dating to the later second millennium BCE.

pl367530812.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl367530812.description: A proto-nuragic settlement on Monte Nuxi that covered approximately one hectare. The remains of various built springs are evident.

pl739961553.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl739961553.description: The Domu de Orgia at Esterzili is the largest nuragic "megaron" structure thus far discovered in Sardinia.

pl149683041.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl835247251.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl93478895.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl625626693.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl625626693.description: A Late Bronze age nuragic complex composed of a central tower, a quadrilobate bastion, and a village.

pl13999296.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl13999296.description: Es Trepucó, Minorca, is the site of a Talaiotic village that dates from 1500 to 1300 BC.

pl411868128.description: A sacred well sanctuary, Pozzo sacro Is Pirois, is associated with the Nuragic culture. Is Pirois is located in the municipality of Villaputzu, in metropolitan Cagliari. The well is built of schist, and the covering structure is a pseudo-dome or tholos.

pl233265929.description: Torre d'en Galmés was a Talaiotic settlement of Bronze Age Minorca and was established ca. 1400 BC.

pl849534583.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl849534583.description: A nuragic complex including a central nuraghe and an associated village.

pl786551142.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl786551142.description: A Nuragic settlement that pre-dates and, in some cases, is re-occupied during the Roman period.

pl43375550.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl43375550.description: Son Mercer de Baix is a naviform settlement on the island of Menorca. These "boat-shaped" stone settlements belong to the prehistoric cultures of the Balearic Islands.

pl712997240.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl655808603.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl471974.description: A Phoenician–Punic and later Roman settlement in southwestern Sardinia, Monte Sirai also has evidence for nuragic settlement during the second millennium BC.

pl460094535.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl460094535.description: A multi-period nuragic site that began as a single tower ca. the Middle Bronze Age (1500 BC).

pl37918020.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl37918020.description: The Punic necropolis at Othoca in Sardinia.

pl265827.description: A pre-Roman and Roman settlement on the island of Majorca. Its ruins are known as Pedret de Bóquer, which is located at the modern Port de Pollença. The original settlement dates ca. 1400 BC.

pl328783231.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl712997241.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl676647078.description: Torrellafuda is the site of a Talayotic settlement on the island of Minorca.

pl142936702.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl142936702.description: Sant Agustí Vell (also known as Poblat talaiòtic de Sant Agustí or "Talayotic village of Sant Agustí") is an archaeological site attributed to the Talayotic culture located in the municipality of Es Migjorn Gran in the south of the Balearic island of Menorca. pl471899.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl471899.description: A city with its origins in a Phoenician settlement of the seventh century BC, Caralis comes under Roman control in 238 BC during the Punic Wars. Florus refers to it as urbs urbinum, or capital of Sardinia.

pl471942.description: The Herakleous Limen, mentioned by Ptolemy, was an ancient bay or anchorage on the island of Sardinia, probably to be identified with the modern Porto Malfatano, which is located on the southern coast of the island between the Capo Malfatano and the Capo Spartivento.

pl472024.description: A site with Phoenician origins (founded ca. 730-700 B.C.) located in southwestern Sardinia. Site of a Roman naval victory against Carthage by Gaius Sulpicius Paterculus in 258 B.C. during the First Punic War.

pl472032.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl472032.description: An ancient Phoenician settlement located in western Sardinia on a promontory in the Gulf of Oristano, just south of modern San Giovanni di Sinis. While it originates as a Punic or Carthaginian settlement ca. 700 BCE, it continued as a major town in Roman times.

pl877459133.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl877459133.description: A fortified Phoenico-Punic settlement on Sardinia with two necropoleis.

The location should lie within a kilometer of the BAtlas coordinates: a point to the northwest of modern Ksar El Abtal and immediately north of Douar Nouaoura in Algeria's Setif Wilaya.

cur-fossil-ain-hanech.dateNote: In 1947 Camille Arambourg found stone tools among the bones of extinct animals at Aïn Hanech, near Sétif in Algeria. They are about 1.8 million years old; tools reported in 2018 from Ain Boucherit, close by, are about 2.4 million years old.
cur-fossil-ain-hanech.summary: An Algerian site showing people made stone tools in North Africa almost 2 million years ago.

cur-fossil-tighennif.dateNote: In 1954 Camille Arambourg, digging a sand pit at Ternifine (now Tighennif), Algeria, found the first of three human jaws with hand axes. He named them Atlanthropus mauritanicus; today they count as Homo erectus or a close relative, about 0.7 million years old.
cur-fossil-tighennif.summary: Three 700,000-year-old human jaws from a sand pit in Algeria.
